# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. Cell Coloring & Shading
Games where cells are marked as shaded/unshaded or colored based on logical constraints.

### A. Pure Shading
- Akari (light bulbs illuminate unshaded cells)
- Hitori (shade duplicate values)
- Kurodoko (shade cells to isolate numbers)
- Kurotto (shade cells around numbered clues)
- Nurikabe (shade cells to form walls around islands)
- Nuritwin (shade cells to create twin regions)

### B. Shading with Path/Region Constraints
- Heyawake (shade cells while maintaining path connectivity)
- Norinori (shade cells in specific patterns per region)
- Nurimisaki (shade cells leaving peninsulas of unshaded cells)
- Satogaeri (shade cells around villages)
- Sto-stone (shade cells to create stone patterns)

### C. Shading with Specific Patterns
- Shakashaka (shade triangular patterns in cells)
- Tilepaint (shade cells to match tile patterns)

## II. Path & Loop Drawing
Games where continuous lines or paths are drawn on the grid.

### A. Single Closed Loop
- Dotchi-Loop (draw loop through specific cells)
- Hebi (draw snake loop)
- Masyu (draw loop through pearls and circles)
- Mid-loop (draw loop with midpoint constraints)
- Slitherlink (draw loop around grid edges)

### B. Multiple Paths/Connections
- Hashiwokakero (draw bridges between islands)
- Numberlink (connect matching numbers with paths)
- Sashigane (draw L-shaped paths)

### C. Flow & Circulation
- Nagareru (create flowing paths)
- Nurimeizu (create maze-like paths)

## III. Polyomino Placement & Tiling
Games involving placement of connected cell groups.

### A. Specific Polyomino Types
- LITS (place L, I, T, S tetrominoes)
- Shikaku (place rectangular regions)

### B. Variable Polyominoes
- Evolomino (place polyominoes of increasing size)
- Fillomino (fill grid with polyominoes matching size clues)
- Five Cells (place pentominoes)

### C. Block-Based Puzzles
- Chained Block (connect and place blocks)
- Choco Banana (place chocolate and banana blocks)
- Double Choco (place two types of chocolate blocks)

## IV. Number & Logic Deduction
Games based on numerical constraints and logical deduction.

### A. Sudoku Variants
- Sudoku (standard number placement)
- Suraromu (Sudoku with irregular regions)

### B. Numerical Path/Region Puzzles
- Juosan (connect numbers in sequence)
- Nansuke (place numbers following clues)
- Ripple Effect (place numbers with distance constraints)
- Yosenabe (group numbers by sum)

### C. Clue-Based Deduction
- Moon-or-Sun (determine cell states from clues)
- Usowan (identify true/false clues)
- Yajilin (shade cells following directional clues)

## V. Hybrid & Specialized
Games combining multiple mechanics or unique rule sets.

### A. Clue Interpretation
- Makaro (interpret ambiguous clues)
- Pencils (place pencils following constraints)
